result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-025-schema.md, closing the schema gap CODE-DESIGNER flagged in docs/agents/design/REQ-025.md Sec1: the new notification_ledger table sendLedgeredNotification (REQ-025.md Sec3.1 step 4) inserts into as the sole idempotency mechanism for AC1/AC2. Read core-directives.md, REQ-025.md in full (CODE-DESIGNER's design), the current apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts (all existing tables, enum precedent, FK convention), and REQ-011.md (this schema's own stated reasoning for pgEnum-vs-text and for audit_log.at's DEFAULT now() precedent) before designing.

Table: notification_ledger -- id (UUID PK), registration_id (UUID NOT NULL FK -> registrations.id ON DELETE RESTRICT, per REQ-025.md Sec1's explicit no-cascade instruction), kind (text NOT NULL), created_at (timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()), updated_at (timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), kept for schema-wide consistency though the row is write-once in practice). UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) is the load-bearing constraint -- the entire mechanism AC1 depends on and the literal thing AC2 tests by direct duplicate insert. No actor/sent-by column (not an audit trail, per REQ-025.md Sec1). No event_id column and no extra index: Sec6 shows REQ-026/027's anticipated per-event anti-join query (registrations LEFT JOIN notification_ledger ON registration_id+kind WHERE event_id=$1 AND ledger row IS NULL) is already served by the UNIQUE constraint's own backing index with registration_id as its leading column -- adding event_id would be unrequested denormalization with a second place for it to drift from registrations.event_id.

kind DECISION: plain `text`, app-validated against the NotificationKind union already specified in REQ-025.md Sec2 (apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts) -- NOT a native pgEnum, despite admission/event_status/event_format's existing pgEnum precedent (REQ-011 Sec2/Sec4). Reasoning: REQ-011's own stated rationale for pgEnum there is a set that is small, closed, and PRD-exhaustive with no expected growth ('the five values are exhaustive by design'). kind is the opposite case on the one fact that matters -- REQ-025.md Sec1 itself names reminder_24h/reminder_3h/event_cancelled as landing 'soon' (REQ-026/027) plus two more Release-3 marketing kinds after that (S10) -- a set growing roughly once per near-term requirement. Under pgEnum, every addition is its own ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE migration (a real Drizzle-generated migration file, decisions/0005, every time); under text, adding a kind is a one-line TypeScript union change with no migration. What pgEnum would buy -- a DB-enforced guarantee against a stray value -- is weakened here because the table has exactly one write path in the whole codebase (the single INSERT in sendLedgeredNotification Sec3.1 step 4), already receiving a compile-time-checked NotificationKind parameter with no string escape hatch; no ad-hoc/admin/bulk writer exists to guard against the way audit_log.payload or registrations.source do. No AC among AC1-AC6 tests kind's DB-level closedness. This mirrors REQ-011 Sec7's own identical precedent for audit_log.action/entity (free text, because new values arrive with new requirements, and constraining to ENUM 'would require an ALTER TYPE for every new audit-worthy action forever'). No DB CHECK(kind IN (...)) added either, matching chapters.code/users.role's existing no-CHECK precedent -- flagged as an open question (Sec7.1) for SECURITY-REVIEWER/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to confirm or override, not resolved by invention.

created_at DECISION and an issue found: CODE-DESIGNER's REQ-025.md Sec1 states the timestamp must be caller-supplied, 'never defaultNow()... matching this schema's decisions/0006 discipline already applied to audit_log.at.' Checked schema.ts line 339 directly: audit_log.at IS `.defaultNow()` -- the opposite of caller-supplied -- and REQ-011.md Sec7 states explicitly why that is correct: DEFAULT now() is appropriate for 'a row recording when it was written,' which is what decisions/0006 does NOT govern (that decision is about a *predicate* evaluated later against a supplied clock, e.g. finished/registration_open/no_show, never about a write-timestamp fact). CODE-DESIGNER's note cites the precedent backwards. Corrected here: created_at is `timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, matching every other table's preamble convention and REQ-011.md Sec7's actual reasoning for audit_log.at -- no separate sent_at/at-distinct-from-created_at column is needed either, since (unlike audit_log) nothing here gives this table's timestamp a semantic distinct from 'when the row was inserted.' Filed as a MINOR issue (schema doc Sec8) so it's fixed at the source; no rework requested on REQ-025.md itself since sendLedgeredNotification's actual logic (Sec3.1) never depended on which timestamp discipline was used.

Migration: single Drizzle-generated CREATE TABLE (per decisions/0005), purely additive -- no existing table altered, no PII column touched, no SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off triggered. Cleanly reversible via DROP TABLE (nothing else references this table; it's the referencing side of its only FK). Added a one-line 'Resolved' cross-reference in docs/agents/design/REQ-025.md Sec1 pointing to the new schema doc -- no other edit to CODE-DESIGNER's design.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-025.md Sec1 misdescribes the audit_log.at precedent when instructing that notification_ledger's timestamp be caller-supplied -- audit_log.at is actually `.defaultNow()` (schema.ts line 339), and REQ-011.md Sec7 explicitly states DEFAULT now() is the correct choice there because it records 'when the row was written,' not a decisions/0006 time-dependent predicate. docs/agents/design/REQ-025-schema.md Sec3/Sec8 corrects this and designs created_at as DEFAULT now() accordingly. Flagged so the source document's citation is fixed rather than propagated to a future reader; no rework of REQ-025.md's actual sendLedgeredNotification logic is needed since it never depended on the timestamp's write mechanism.

docs/agents/design/REQ-025-schema.md Sec7 open question 1: no DB-level CHECK(kind IN (...)) constraint is added alongside the text column, matching chapters.code/users.role's existing no-CHECK precedent. Declined as unrequested DB enforcement given the sole writer is already compile-time-checked and no AC tests DB-level kind closedness. Flagged for SECURITY-REVIEWER/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to confirm or override, not resolved by invention here.
